question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> be twice differentiable even functions on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mn>1</mn></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mfenced><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mfenced><mn>1</mn></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> Then, the minimum number of solutions of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>"</mo></msup><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>'</mo><mo>'</mo></mrow></msup><mfenced><mi>x</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to _____.

solution.text:
Let hx=fxg'x roots
∵ fx is even ⇒f14=f12=f-12=f14=0 and gx has two roots as g34=g-34=0 (as gx is even function)

So, hx=fxg'x will have 5 roots, hence its derivative h'x=fxg"x+f'xg'x will have 4 roots.
